boundary_condition: Apply only to hotel room bed configuration, not to destination, dates, room count, amenities such as balcony or view, or non-hotel travel choices.
condition: When booking or comparing hotel rooms where bed type can be selected.
default_action: Look for or request a king-size bed before other bed sizes; if a king room is not available within the current hotel constraints, allow a queen-size bed as the fallback.
exception_condition: If the current request explicitly asks for queen-size or another bed arrangement, or only queen-size options satisfy the other required hotel constraints, follow that bed arrangement instead of insisting on king-size.
name: Request king-size hotel bed first
preference_value: king-size bed, with queen-size acceptable fallback
rationale: Across independent hotel examples, king-size appears as a desired or acceptable bed type, often alongside queen-size as an acceptable alternative. The most coherent reusable default is to prefer king-size while not treating queen-size as disqualifying.

source_evidence.contribution: Said, "I need a queen-sized bed, preferably king size," grounding king-size as preferred with queen-size as an acceptable fallback.
Said they would prefer a room with a "king size or queen size bed," grounding both bed sizes as acceptable with king included.
Asked for one bedroom and said it "could be a queen size or a king size," grounding queen-or-king flexibility for hotel bed configuration.
Said, "we're going to need a king-size bed," grounding an explicit king-size bed request.

I would prefer the one with king size or queen size bed in the room.
